acceptance_criteria: With a physical keyboard or controlled keyboard input and no pointer, open a synthetic book from the shelf, navigate its contents, search for a term, open a note and return to reading: all required commands are reachable and focus is always identifiable.
Assign one key to two incompatible reader actions: the binding editor explains the conflict before application and provides a keyboard-reachable restore-defaults action.
Use a named Android switch-access configuration to traverse a popup and dismiss it: focus returns to the invoking control, and a remapped page-turn key does not turn pages while entering note text.
limitations: Existing keyboard coverage, remapping conflicts and switch-access behavior were not tested. Readest's support statement is documentation only and does not prove equivalent behavior on every platform.

proposals.title: Make background TTS interruption and media-control policy predictable
proposals.existing_capability: Moon already provides TTS, background speech and headset/Bluetooth controls. Its FAQ specifically discusses screen-off interruptions and battery restrictions affecting both the reader and speech engine.
proposals.rationale: User pause, competing audio, route disconnection and OS/engine suspension have different recovery expectations. The existing background workflow needs an observable policy rather than a generic instruction to change every battery setting.
proposals.requested_change: Apply a documented audio-focus and route-change policy consistently across reader, notification and headset controls, preserve explicit user pause, and expose the last known interruption reason with app-versus-engine diagnostic context.
acceptance_criteria: On a declared Android/engine combination permitting background playback, narrate a synthetic document for ten minutes with the screen off: foreground and notification controls agree on playback state, and any interruption has a recorded reason or explicitly unknown cause.

Request exclusive audio focus from a controlled second player, then release it: TTS follows the displayed pause/resume policy; an explicit user Pause during that interruption prevents automatic restart.

Disconnect a test headset while speaking under the pause-on-disconnect policy: speech stops within a proposed one-second budget and does not unexpectedly continue through the speaker; reconnecting preserves the explicit paused state.
limitations: No speech interruption or media-control defect was reproduced. Device battery policy and speech-engine behavior can limit background operation; the duration and response budget are prospective tests, not promises for every Android device.

proposals.title: Resolve TTS language and offline voice availability explicitly
proposals.existing_capability: Moon already advertises support for TTS engines and multilingual reading; the baseline distinguishes engine availability and text extraction from the existence of the speech feature.
proposals.rationale: A selected engine may lack the publication's language or require a network voice. Explicit resolution and fallback make multilingual and offline reading predictable without implying Moon ships every voice.
proposals.requested_change: Show the resolved engine, voice, language and known offline requirement, allow per-book language/voice corrections, and explain unavailable voices before starting with an explicit user-approved fallback.
acceptance_criteria: Narrate a synthetic EPUB with English and German language-tagged passages using installed test voices: the selected policy chooses the intended voice for each passage or clearly identifies a fixed-voice override.

Disable networking with only a network-required voice selected: the reader explains the requirement and offers an installed offline alternative when available instead of silently entering a playing state with no output.

Remove the preferred test voice and reopen the book: the unavailable selection is identified, the chosen fallback is displayed, and a per-book correction does not change another book's voice preferences.
limitations: Current voice selection, language inheritance and offline indicators were not exercised. Engines may expose incomplete voice/network metadata; unknown capability should be labeled rather than treated as a verified offline guarantee.

proposals.title: Keep narration position and sentence navigation synchronized
proposals.existing_capability: Moon already documents ebook/PDF speech and configurable hands-free controls; this proposal refines the relationship between spoken position, reading position and navigation.
proposals.rationale: Browsing visually while listening, changing typography and skipping a sentence should not leave the displayed passage tied to a stale utterance. The reviewed calibre guide documents speech highlighting as a workflow reference.
proposals.requested_change: Maintain a source-anchored narration cursor distinct from optional visual browsing, expose previous/next sentence and return-to-spoken-passage actions, and discard stale progress callbacks after a speech jump or document change.
acceptance_criteria: Narrate a synthetic EPUB and text PDF with uniquely numbered sentences: Previous sentence repeats the expected sentence and Next sentence starts the following one, with the displayed speech marker matching the actual submitted utterance.

While paused mid-document, change font size or orientation and browse elsewhere: Return to speech restores the narration sentence, and resuming follows the documented sentence-boundary policy rather than the new visual position.
Delay a progress callback, jump to sentence 20 and resume, then release the old callback: it cannot move the speech marker or playback back to the abandoned sentence or a previously closed book.
limitations: Current Moon speech-navigation controls and progress mapping were not tested. Calibre highlighting is documented rather than measured here; engines without fine-grained timing need an explicitly coarser marker. Over-limit text completeness remains MOON-005.

proposals.title: Reconcile Pro privacy disclosures by actual data flow
proposals.existing_capability: Moon already publishes a Pro-specific privacy policy and describes user-selected cloud synchronization. The official-source baseline records MD-01 as a wording discrepancy between collection-denial statements and third-party/log-data language.
proposals.rationale: Readers need to distinguish developer-operated collection, optional third-party services and transfers they request to their own cloud. Conflicting policy language warrants clarification without inferring undisclosed traffic.
proposals.requested_change: Publish a dated, Pro-specific data-flow inventory identifying which statements apply to each optional feature, the data and recipient involved, retention/deletion behavior and available controls, and reconcile it with store disclosures and in-app explanations.
acceptance_criteria: For cloud sync, external dictionary/translation and any diagnostics actually present, the published inventory identifies whether data leaves the device, the recipient category, relevant fields, trigger and retention/control policy; absent or unknown flows are not invented.

Compare the Pro policy's collection summary with its third-party and Log Data sections and the store disclosure: each statement has an explicit, consistent scope and the document carries a revision date.
Follow each documented optional-flow control in the named Pro build: its label and explanation match the inventory, and unsupported controls are not described as available.
limitations: MD-01 is documentation evidence, not a verified telemetry defect or legal finding. No network capture or token-storage audit supports this proposal; the combined free/Pro policy cannot alone establish an SDK or data flow in Pro.

proposals.title: Support selected-file and folder access for core reading tasks
proposals.existing_capability: Moon already provides file management, PDF annotation saving and backup/export. Play and the Pro policy explain broad storage access for those workflows; availability of a folder-scoped alternative was not established.
proposals.rationale: Someone reading a chosen folder should be able to understand which tasks require broader access. A smaller optional permission scope can improve trust while preserving an explicit full-library management choice.
proposals.requested_change: Provide a clearly documented selected-file/folder workflow for opening, organizing references to and exporting accessible books, with explicit read-only versus writable destination handling and task-specific explanations when broader access is genuinely required.
acceptance_criteria: With All Files Access denied on a declared Android version, select one synthetic-book folder: supported books can be opened and annotated within the documented scope, and an unrelated unselected folder is not indexed by this workflow.

Open a read-only provider PDF and save an annotated copy to a separately selected writable destination: the original is unchanged, the copy is readable, and the UI identifies both access scopes accurately.
Export notes or a backup to a selected destination, then revoke its grant: the next write requests repair for that destination without representing an unrelated broad permission as already granted.
limitations: Existing scoped-access routes and actual permission use were not tested; published permission explanations do not prove unnecessary access. Android/provider capabilities vary, and recovery of existing unavailable locations is separately covered by MOON-048.

proposals.title: Protect backup and sync packages independently of startup lock
proposals.existing_capability: Moon already advertises password/fingerprint startup protection, backup/restore and cloud synchronization. App locking does not by itself establish encryption of backup or cloud packages.
proposals.rationale: Confidentiality of a copied backup or cloud annotation package is a separate boundary from access to the running app. The desired property should be explicit and compatible with the user's recovery and interoperability needs.
proposals.requested_change: Evaluate opt-in authenticated encryption for Moon-managed backups and reading-state/annotation sync packages, with documented device enrollment, recovery and exposed metadata. Label encrypted packages distinctly from ordinary book files and interoperable exports.
acceptance_criteria: Create an encrypted synthetic backup containing a unique note sentinel: an independent package inspection cannot recover its protected text without the key, while an authorized second disposable profile restores the exact covered content and manifest.
Use an incorrect recovery secret and a separately bit-flipped package: each is rejected with an authentication/integrity error before replacing live library state.

Enroll a second test client, rotate the shared protection key and restore with the documented recovery material: authorized clients recover the same note revision, and the UI lists metadata or ordinary book files outside the encryption scope.
limitations: Current availability needs checking: no existing encryption or key-storage design was inspected, so this is not a claim that current payloads are plaintext. Encryption design, recovery security and older-client compatibility require focused review; a sentinel search alone would not establish cryptographic security.

proposals.title: Reduce cold-open time to the first usable reading passage
proposals.existing_capability: Moon already advertises broad-format reading and smooth scrolling; the baseline contains no measured open latency or large-document advantage. The reviewed Librera work identifies separate opening/indexing stages as a profiling reference.
proposals.rationale: Time to display a page, time until it accepts input and completion of background indexing are different user-visible costs. Optimizing a measured critical path avoids trading a fast splash screen for a blocked reader.
proposals.requested_change: Instrument open-to-first-readable and open-to-interactive milestones by format/cache state, prioritize the requested passage over nonessential indexing, and adopt changes only after comparable baseline/candidate measurements preserve rendering and position fidelity.
acceptance_criteria: On one declared device/build configuration, record twenty cold and twenty warm opens of each named synthetic PDF/EPUB with fixed hashes/settings, reporting p50/p95 readable and interactive latency separately from indexing completion.

For a measured slow case selected before optimization, the candidate reduces cold-open p95 interactive latency by a proposed 20 percent while warm-open p95 worsens by no more than 10 percent and the same source passage/annotations remain visible.

Cancel a deliberately delayed open and select a second book: the second reader becomes usable without an eventual callback navigating back to the abandoned book, and the timing record includes cancellation cleanup.
limitations: No Moon performance regression or timing baseline was measured. Counts and percentage budgets are proposed acceptance targets; Librera's reported loading issue does not demonstrate a Moon bottleneck or justify a predetermined optimization.

proposals.title: Bound retained document resources across repeated reading sessions
proposals.existing_capability: Moon already renders multiple document formats, supports PDF annotations and maintains a library with cover caches; cache rebuilding is an existing documented operation.
proposals.rationale: Useful caching and resources accidentally retained after a document closes have different lifetimes. A repeatable retention budget can guide cleanup without alleging a leak from code size or a single memory reading.
proposals.requested_change: Measure per-document memory, file/render handles and cache retention across open/use/close cycles, bound caches by a declared policy, and release closed-document work on success, failure and cancellation while preserving persistent annotations.
acceptance_criteria: Run fifty open/navigate/annotate/close cycles over a fixed ten-document synthetic corpus on a declared device, recording managed/native memory and open-handle counts after the same cleanup window each cycle; after warmup, the final ten-cycle retained-memory median stays within a proposed 10 percent of the preceding ten-cycle median and handle counts do not grow per cycle.

Inject a document-open failure and cancel a pending render in separate cycles: resources return within the declared cleanup window and a different book opens normally without the failed document remaining active.

Evict the document/cover caches under the chosen storage budget and reopen: saved notes and positions remain intact, required caches rebuild, and the measured cache size returns within its declared bound.
limitations: No memory leak, cache corruption or handle-growth measurement was made. The proposed plateau check is a bounded regression test, not proof that all lifetime leaks are absent; device allocator behavior and cache warmup must be recorded.

proposals.title: Offer a measured low-refresh reading profile for e-ink screens
proposals.existing_capability: Moon already offers themes, page animations, auto-scroll and extensive input controls. KOReader's reviewed README documents an animation-free, e-ink-oriented interface as a comparison point.
proposals.rationale: A coordinated low-refresh preset can reduce unnecessary repainting and improve legibility on supported e-ink hardware without requiring users to discover each independent setting.
proposals.requested_change: Provide a reversible low-refresh preset that coordinates motion, contrast and status-update frequency, and expose hardware refresh options only where the device actually supports them; measure redraw and energy effects before advertising benefits.
acceptance_criteria: Enable the preset and turn sixty pages of a fixed synthetic EPUB/PDF corpus: page transitions avoid intermediate animation frames, reading controls retain clear selected states, and disabling the preset restores the user's prior settings.

On a declared supported e-ink test device, compare the same scripted workload with the ordinary profile and report redraw counts, ghosting observations and energy measurements with uncertainty; publish no battery-improvement claim unsupported by those results.
Open the preset on a device without a supported full-refresh interface: unsupported hardware actions are labeled unavailable while the ordinary low-motion/contrast controls remain usable.
limitations: Existing Moon e-ink presets and refresh integrations were not inspected; no e-ink or energy test was run. KOReader's positioning is documentation rather than a measured head-to-head advantage, and emulator output cannot establish physical ghosting or energy use.

proposals.title: Prepare minimal redacted diagnostics for a chosen support problem
proposals.existing_capability: Moon already advertises customer email support and publishes a FAQ covering speech, export, sync and rendering settings. The reviewed sources do not establish a mandatory report template or verified in-app reporting menu.
proposals.rationale: A report needs the relevant build, mode and outcome without exposing the user's entire library or cloud credentials. A previewable diagnostic summary can make a narrowly scoped support conversation reproducible.
proposals.requested_change: Offer an optional problem-specific diagnostic summary with build/OS, relevant mode or engine, last operation outcome and user-entered reproduction steps; preview and redact it locally before saving or explicitly sharing through the published support route.
acceptance_criteria: Prepare separate synthetic TTS, PDF-save and sync reports: each contains the named build/OS, relevant engine/mode and operation outcome, while unknown values remain explicitly unknown rather than guessed.

Seed the test profile with canary credentials, private-looking filenames and unrelated note text: none appears in the default diagnostic output; an explicitly selected synthetic fixture is listed separately with its hash and attachment choice.
Edit the preview, cancel sharing and reopen it: no submission has occurred, the draft remains recoverable locally, and a later explicit export contains exactly the approved fields.
limitations: Current diagnostics or in-app support tools were not established, so this does not declare them absent. No report was submitted by this proposal; automatic secret removal would require explicit adversarial tests before being treated as complete.

proposals.title: Publish a versioned format-by-mode capability and fallback matrix
proposals.existing_capability: Moon already publishes broad format lists, PDF forms/annotations, EPUB3 media and table-preview guidance. Its FAQ explicitly states that DRM-protected books are unsupported.
proposals.rationale: A supported extension does not promise every speech, selection, form or media workflow for every file. A mode-aware matrix would prevent avoidable support ambiguity and help users reach existing fallbacks.
proposals.requested_change: Publish a build/edition-scoped matrix separating document rendering, text extraction, speech, annotation, form and media behavior, with prerequisites, exact entrypoints and explicit supported/conditional/unsupported/unknown labels linked to fallback guidance.
acceptance_criteria: Look up a searchable PDF, image-only PDF, EPUB3 media book and DRM-protected EPUB: each row separately identifies viewing, text-dependent actions and any compatibility limitation, without treating a filename extension as proof that every action works.
Follow the table-layout fallback from the matrix in the named build: it reaches the documented publisher-formatting preview, and PDF form support states which field families were actually checked.
For every cell labeled tested, the matrix links a build, synthetic fixture and dated result; documented-only and untested mode combinations remain visibly different from executed passes.
limitations: A complete current publisher matrix was not established in the bounded baseline review; that does not prove none exists. This is a documentation/referral contract, not a request to remove DRM or to declare every format fully conformant.

proposals.title: Publish build-specific changes with traceable resolution status
proposals.existing_capability: Moon already publishes Play release notes; the dated baseline records five v10.8 changes, including embedded-font CSS improvements, double-tap zoom and missing-file relinking. A complete official history was not recovered.
proposals.rationale: Users checking whether a reported interaction changed need edition/build context and a stable reference. A note saying optimized or fixed should not imply independent verification on all documents or devices.
proposals.requested_change: Maintain a searchable, stable-linked changelog identifying edition, version/build and publication date, with affected workflows and known conditions. Where a support problem is referenced, distinguish a claimed fix, a shipped fix and a separately recorded reproduction/retest result.
acceptance_criteria: Locate the v10.8 entries by searching for relink, zoom and embedded font: stable links identify the relevant changes and preserve the distinction between listing update date and a verified release/build date.

For one synthetic support case used to demonstrate the process, follow its changelog reference: the affected and candidate-fixed build, remaining conditions and retest status are visible without exposing a private email thread.
Publish a subsequent entry without overwriting the earlier one: both remain independently addressable, and an untested claimed fix is not labeled independently verified.
limitations: The existing release-history and support-status coverage was a bounded documentation search, not proof of absence. No official public tracker or response SLA was established, and this proposal does not invent either one.
